item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Clear Selected Desk Clutter

turns.text: Remove the papers and the empty takeaway cup from this desk photo. Leave the laptop, coffee mug and cables alone.

item.tests: Tests selective clutter removal without deleting nearby objects the user explicitly wants retained.

answer_sheet.Objects to remove: The papers and the empty takeaway cup only.
answer_sheet.Objects to keep: Keep the laptop, coffee mug and tangled cables in their original positions.
answer_sheet.Style and size: Natural photo edit, original wide framing, free-tier resolution.

must_haves: The papers and empty takeaway cup are absent.
The laptop, coffee mug and tangled cables remain visibly intact in their original positions.
Exposed desk areas have believable surface texture and lighting, without leftover object fragments.
The original wide framing and surrounding home-office scene are preserved.

turns.text: Remove the papers and the empty takeaway cup from this desk pic. Leave the laptop, coffee mug and cables alone. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
The cheapest listed option is **Flux 2 Klein, one image at 640px, starting at 5 credits**. It’s available on your free plan. I can’t verify a live final price or your balance with the tools available here, so that’s a listed price—not a guaranteed quote.

I’d remove the papers in the foreground and behind the laptop, plus the disposable cup on the right, while preserving the **laptop, ceramic coffee mug, and cables**.

- **Smaller/cheaper:** 640px is the lowest supported setting and is already larger than this 512px-wide photo. No cheaper AI-edit option is listed.
- **Shorter:** Duration doesn’t apply to a still-image edit.
- **Zero-credit alternative:** Manual clone/heal editing in a photo editor.

**Nothing has run or spent credits.** Would you like to proceed with the lowest-cost listed option, or avoid spending credits?

turns.agent:
The edit was refused because your account has **insufficient credits**. This was a dry run: **no image was generated and no credits were spent**.

I won’t retry or switch tools. The zero-credit alternative is to use a manual healing/clone tool to remove the papers and disposable cup, carefully preserving the laptop, ceramic mug, and cables.

Preserve all other objects, the composition, camera angle, lighting and photographic appearance. Do not remove the ceramic mug or change any cables.
